# DECISION_LOG

## How to read this file

Each row is a decision the project has made. The four columns
hold *receipts*: a one- or two-sentence prose cell each. Detail
belongs in the linked RFC and any associated build handoff,
not in the row itself.

The cell budget exists so the log stays a navigable receipt and
does not grow back into duplicated SPEC content. Newer rows are
expected to honor the budget; older rows may be grandfathered.

## How to add a row

1. Pick the next sequential ID (`D###`).
2. Write the four cells:
   - **Decision** — what we decided. Imperative, present tense.
   - **Context** — why we needed to decide. The tension we
     were resolving.
   - **Consequence** — what changes as a result. Cite the RFC
     and any code/test entry points.
   - **Revisit** — the conditions that would justify reopening
     this decision.
3. Cite the RFC and (when applicable) a build handoff or PR.

| D002 | accepted | Expand the PRD scope to absorb RFCs 0005–0008. Hydrostatics, analytical resistance estimation (Michell + ITTC), a portable browser frontend, and a headless CLI are *in scope*. The out-of-scope list is reduced to four genuine domain boundaries (full-boat solid, structural, outfitting, non-kayak hulls). | The original PRD was drafted before the project's direction expanded toward generative CFD evaluation. Leaving that contradiction in place forces every future contributor (human or agent) to read the PRD with a footnote, and risks re-litigation of decisions the RFC trail has already settled. | `docs/PRD.md` rewritten: audience and in-scope sections describe the full pipeline (geometry + hydrostatics + resistance + desktop + web); out-of-scope list restricted to true non-goals; success criteria added for hydrostatic accuracy, resistance fidelity, and URL-shareable hulls. `AGENTS.md` no longer needs a "where the docs and the RFCs disagree" section. | If a future RFC moves a currently-in-scope item back out (e.g., resistance estimation proves unsalvageably inaccurate at the live tier), or if the project narrows its audience back to "geometry only." |
